current_row.boundary_rationale: The petition opens with an imperative addressed directly to Yahweh, "הַבֵּ֤ט מִשָּׁמַ֨יִם֙" (oshb:Isa.63.15, byte tier) ('Look down from heaven'), rendered “Look down from heaven, and see” (web:Isa.63.15) -- a tier-1 vocative/imperative onset per the addressee-shift class, distinct from the third-person recollection that precedes it. The petition runs through the single MT verse that spans two WEB verses: the never-ruled complaint "הָיִ֗ינוּ מֵֽעוֹלָם֙ לֹֽא מָשַׁ֣לְתָּ בָּ֔ם לֹֽא נִקְרָ֥א שִׁמְךָ֖ עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם" (oshb:Isa.63.19, byte tier) lives at web:Isa.63.19 ('we have become like those from of old you never ruled, your name not called upon them'), and the same MT verse's tear-the-heavens plea "לוּא קָרַ֤עְתָּ שָׁמַ֨יִם֙ יָרַ֔דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ" (oshb:Isa.63.19, byte tier) lives at web:Isa.64.1 ('oh that you would tear the heavens, you would come down, the mountains would quake'); both halves belong to this row because they are one Hebrew sentence sharing one verse's bytes, and a row boundary is not argued between them. The theophany imagery continues past the split (fire kindling brushwood, the nations trembling, mountains quaking again at 64:2-3) and the unit closes at the affirmation "לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔" (oshb:Isa.64.3, byte tier) (web:Isa.64.4, 'the eye has not seen a God besides you'), immediately before the confessional turn “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5) opens a different speech-act.

Held at medium_low confidence and flagged as a genuine frontier question because the exact seam separating petition-recollection from confession is argued from a rhetorical-mode shift rather than a formal header, and because this row carries the book's one split-verse pair (MT 63:19 = web:Isa.63.19 + web:Isa.64.1): every reference to either half above names which half it lives in, and the two halves are not treated as separable content. The theophany phrase 'the mountains quaked' recurs near-verbatim across the split (web:Isa.64.1's mountain-quaking wish and web:Isa.64.3's mountain-quaking report), a byte-true echo disclosed here rather than argued as a boundary.

items.claim: The row's prose carries two bare, witness-unqualified chapter-and-verse coordinates inside offset zone B, where the same numerals denote different verses in the two witnesses.
items.proposed_change: Field repair: qualify both prose coordinates (web:Isa.64.2-Isa.64.3 (MT 64:1-64:2) and web:Isa.64.5 (MT 64:4)) to match the disclosure already used elsewhere in the row.
items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes and the staged crosswalk; every run below collates at byte tier. The row's boundary_rationale writes 'mountains quaking again at 64:2-3' and its strongest_rejected_alternative 'the confessional turn at 64:5' with no witness prefix and no numeric qualifier, inside zone B where the crosswalk maps WEB 64:2, 64:3 and 64:5 to MT 64:1, 64:2 and 64:4. Under the book-wide convention that bare coordinates are WEB, both are content-correct: web:Isa.64.2 (MT 64:1) carries the kindling fire and the trembling nations, כִּקְדֹ֧חַ אֵ֣שׁ הֲמָסִ֗ים (oshb:Isa.64.1 = web:Isa.64.2, byte tier) and מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ גּוֹיִ֥ם יִרְגָּֽזוּ (oshb:Isa.64.1 = web:Isa.64.2, byte tier); web:Isa.64.3 (MT 64:2) carries the second mountain-quaking report יָרַ֕דְתָּ מִפָּנֶ֖יךָ הָרִ֥ים נָזֹֽלּוּ (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, byte tier); and web:Isa.64.5 (MT 64:4) carries the confession הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier). Read as MT numbers they fail: oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4 opens וּמֵעוֹלָ֥ם (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier) and runs to the incomparability affirmation עַ֣יִן לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier), not a quaking report, and MT 64:5 = web:Isa.64.6 is a different confession verse. So the defect is real: two zone-B coordinates in prose do not name their numbering space, against the rule that any digit touching chs 63-64 names it, in the row that carries the split verse and that otherwise dual-qualifies every structured ref. Tested the other way, against the finding: nothing in the row is byte-false, both coordinates resolve correctly under the governing convention, the row's boundary_evidence_refs and device_notes carry arithmetically correct duals, and no seam depends on either coordinate; the ambiguity is one of labeling, which the severity law places at low (disclosure shortfall), not a defective digit claim. Noted without effect on the verdict: the finding's own Hebrew citations are unfilled percent-s placeholders, so its byte grounds were re-derived here rather than trusted. Downgraded to low.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived from bytes; every run below collates at byte tier. MT 64:4 (= web:Isa.64.5 by the crosswalk) carries its athnach (U+0591) on its seventh token יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier); the half before it, פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), is a 2ms verb with 2ms suffixes continuing the address to Yahweh from עַ֣יִן לֹֽא רָאָ֗תָה אֱלֹהִים֙ זוּלָ֣תְךָ֔ (oshb:Isa.64.3 = web:Isa.64.4, byte tier), rendered “You meet him who rejoices and does righteousness, those who remember you in your ways.” (web:Isa.64.5); the self-accusation הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier), whose וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, byte tier) is the verse's first first-person-plural form, stands only after that caesura, rendered “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5). The row closes 'immediately before the confessional turn ... (web:Isa.64.5) opens a different speech-act' and its rejected alternative treats 'the confessional turn at 64:5' as the whole verse's mode, so the rear-seam driver is presented as verse-initial when half a verse of the row's own second-person petition mode intervenes between the row's close and the turn; the book-order neighbor row discloses the mid-verse onset explicitly and this row does not. Tested the other way, against the finding: rows are verse-granular, web:Isa.64.4 = oshb:Isa.64.3 is the nearest verse boundary before the turn, and the paragraph-mark inventory carries no mark at MT 64:3 or 64:4, so the placement stands and no respan is implied; the defect is a mis-presented driver position in a medium_low, frontier-flagged row whose seam is argued from exactly that rhetorical-mode shift, a defective warrant not alone load-bearing: medium as filed.

current_row.boundary_rationale: The confession turns on a self-accusation standing mid-verse, after the verse's own caesura at יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier), whose first half, פָּגַ֤עְתָּ אֶת שָׂשׂ֙ וְעֹ֣שֵׂה צֶ֔דֶק בִּדְרָכֶ֖יךָ יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier), is second-person address continuing the preceding praise: "הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א" (oshb:Isa.64.4, byte tier) (web:Isa.64.5, 'Behold, you were angry, and we sinned'), a first-person-plural admission that has no counterpart in the preceding petition/recollection panel. The unit develops the confession -- “we have all become like one who is unclean, and all our righteousness is like a polluted garment” (web:Isa.64.6) -- and moves to a closing series of direct imperative pleas, “Don't be furious, Yahweh. Don't remember iniquity forever.” (web:Isa.64.9), reporting the ruined holy cities and temple (web:Isa.64.10 = oshb:Isa.64.9 through web:Isa.64.11 = oshb:Isa.64.10) before closing on a final unanswered double question, “Will you hold yourself back for these things, Yahweh? Will you keep silent and punish us very severely?” (web:Isa.64.12). The unit ends there because oshb:Isa.65.1 answers this very question with a first-person divine reply, a scene and speaker change that the paragraph-mark inventory also brackets: a SAMEKH break sits at this unit's own close (oshb:Isa.64.11 = web:Isa.64.12).

items.claim: The front-seam warrant's own contrast is not byte-supported: the 'second-person address' versus 'first-person-plural admission' opposition fails because the second half of the same verse opens on second-person address too, and first-person-plural verbs already stand in the preceding panel.

items.adjudicator_grounds: Re-derived at byte tier from oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 (14 tokens; atnach on token 7, יִזְכְּר֑וּךָ): the second half opens on הֵן אַתָּ֤ה קָצַ֨פְתָּ֙ (tokens 8-10), second-person address in the same person as the first half's opening verb פָּגַ֤עְתָּ (token 1), so the person of address does not change across the caesura; the only new element is the first-person-plural confession verb וַֽנֶּחֱטָ֔א (token 11), WEB “Behold, you were angry, and we sinned.” (web:Isa.64.5 = oshb:Isa.64.4). First-person-plural verbs already stand inside the preceding row's span: הָיִ֗ינוּ (oshb:Isa.63.19 = web:Isa.63.19, the split verse's first half, token 1; WEB “We have become”) and נְקַוֶּ֑ה (oshb:Isa.64.2 = web:Isa.64.3, token 4; WEB “we didn’t look for”) -- no morphology layer is staged, so the form class rests on the pointed bytes plus both witnesses' renderings. Tested the other way, the row's underlying seam fact holds: skeleton-tier sweeps of the sin, iniquity and transgression roots spliced from oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5, oshb:Isa.64.5 = web:Isa.64.6 and oshb:Isa.59.20 return 23, 16 and 18 verses book-wide with none inside oshb:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.3 (= web:Isa.63.15-Isa.64.4), so the confession onset at oshb:Isa.64.4 = web:Isa.64.5 survives and the finding is right to leave the span alone. The warrant's stated contrast (second-person address versus first-person-plural admission) is byte-defective as a distinguishing ground, while the seam does not rest on that contrast alone: medium, as filed. Non-span item; the proposed field repair (rest the contrast on the confession verb alone and drop the person-shift framing) is consistent with the bytes.

Will you keep silent and punish us very severely?” (web:Isa.64.12 = oshb:Isa.64.11) with two question marks, and that WEB run is the row's only citation for its 'final unanswered double question' and for the observed_substrate_signals entry speech_formula.unanswered_closing_question: the row splices no Hebrew at its own closing verse and none at oshb:Isa.65.1, whose verse-initial first-person form נִדְרַ֨שְׁתִּי֙ (byte tier) is the actual tier-1 speaker change it invokes. Non-span item; the proposed field repair (splice the particle and atnach position, or re-label the signal key) is consistent with the bytes.

current_row.boundary_rationale: A second, formally distinct koh-amar frame opens the unit, "לָכֵ֞ן כֹּה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֗ה" (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) (web:Isa.65.13, 'therefore, thus says the Lord Yahweh'), a different divine-title form (adonai Yahweh) from the 65:8 frame's bare Yahweh. The oracle runs a fourfold contrast formula opened each time by הִנֵּ֨ה עֲבָדַ֤י (oshb:Isa.65.13, byte tier) -- three further instances, הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י and הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י (oshb:Isa.65.13) and הִנֵּ֧ה עֲבָדַ֛י (oshb:Isa.65.14), byte-identical to each other and skeleton-identical to the first (sweep: 4 occurrences over 2 verses) -- “Behold, my servants will eat, but you will be hungry; behold, my servants will drink, but you will be thirsty. Behold, my servants will rejoice, but you will be disappointed.” (web:Isa.65.13) plus a fourth pairing at 65:14 -- and closes at “because the former troubles are forgotten, and because they are hidden from my eyes.” (web:Isa.65.16), immediately before the unit ends and a new declaration, “For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth” (web:Isa.65.17), opens a different oracle on a different subject (cosmic renewal rather than the servants/apostates contrast).

current_row.boundary_rationale: An imperative summons opens the unit, "שִׁמְעוּ֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה" (oshb:Isa.66.5, byte tier) (web:Isa.66.5, 'Hear Yahweh’s word'), rendered “Hear Yahweh’s word, you who tremble at his word” (web:Isa.66.5), addressed to the faithful against their mockers. It moves through a theophany of recompense (66:6) into the sudden, unlabored birth of Zion -- “Before she travailed, she gave birth. Before her pain came, she delivered a son.” (web:Isa.66.7) -- and closes at “Shall I who cause to give birth shut the womb?” says your God.” (web:Isa.66.9), matching "אָמַ֥ר אֱלֹהָֽיִךְ" (oshb:Isa.66.9, byte tier) -- the Elohim variant of the postpositive speech signature, verse-final, its final token carrying no dividing accent; the disclosure inventory records a SAMEKH break at this same closing verse. The unit ends there because 66:10 opens a new imperative summons of its own, “Rejoice with Jerusalem” (web:Isa.66.10).
